grh_564332833b332cd7212f.title: The Waltz of Death
paragraphs: In Vienna, a new waltz by the composer Horvat becomes linked to a series of murders of beautiful women. Herr Gruning had confessed to shooting Princess Stephanie, but officials dismissed him as an egomaniac and released him; he had in fact killed her. The later murders have a different culprit. Holmes realizes the killer must always be armed and that the music itself triggers him, pointing to police chief Count von Rofrano. Rofrano had loved Stephanie, and her death in his arms shattered his mind; whenever he hears the waltz he is driven to destroy other beauty. Holmes has the forbidden music played at a public gathering and watches Rofrano reach for his revolver. Exposed, the count turns the weapon on himself, while Gruning is returned to prison for Stephanie's murder.

grh_56bd0231870b05db2948.title: Cora Plummer Quincy
paragraphs: When Cora Plummer Quincy is wounded by her new husband Oliver's gun, her son Cal becomes suspicious, especially after learning that Oliver does not own the prosperous ranch Cora claimed he had. Britt and Doc Early discover that the apparent deception is Cora's, not Oliver's: after her first husband Ned died, she wanted companionship but feared people would think Oliver had married a wealthy widow for her money, so she invented a fortune for him. The shooting proves accidental, Cal accepts the marriage, and Oliver eventually makes himself an able partner in running the Plummer ranch.

grh_567801e15533c6c2919e.title: Frederika
paragraphs: Young Johann Wolfgang Goethe falls in love with Frederika while living in Sesenheim, and for a time both imagine a simple life together. When an opportunity arrives that could launch the literary career he longs for, Frederika realizes that keeping him in the village would destroy the future he is meant to have and lets him go. Years later the celebrated Goethe returns and learns that Frederika never married. Their love has endured, but she asks him not to turn memory into a new promise, and they part again with their old happiness preserved.

grh_56395a48bd53b23e210d.title: The Afro-Westerner
paragraphs: Joseph Jenkins Roberts leaves Liberia for Wyoming Territory in 1875, carrying family stories of grandparents who had escaped American slavery and a determination to experience the West for himself. In Laramie he befriends a reporter, a boarding-house keeper, a Chinese businessman and Shoshone people, learns to ride and gradually sheds his tenderfoot status. After returning from a family visit with an inheritance, he chooses to work as a cowboy before using the money to buy land and cattle. He eventually marries Moon Feather and builds a ranching life with her, raising six Afro-Indian children near the country his grandparents once knew.
